messages:
kai (eng-infra): Heads-up — billing-bot just fired a high-severity alert: ~4.4x GPU pool spend increase in us-west2 since 03:10 UTC. Can someone check autoscaler provisioning?

billing-bot: ALERT: project:redwood-prod — GPU_POOL_US-WEST2 spend +340% over 1h vs baseline; estimated overage $9.6k. Triggered at 2026-03-18T03:24:12Z

ashwin (sre): On it. Quick question — is this the reserved (dedicated) pool or preemptible spot fleet?

kai (eng-infra): This is the ephemeral autoscale pool used for inference-burst. Should be T4 family, preemptible. Logs show a bunch of new nodes with hostname prefix gpu-a2-..

ryan (infra): I see the same in GCE console — instances launched as a2-highmem-16g with A100-ish profile (expensive) instead of nvidia-t4-standard-8. Terraform drift?

marta (oncall): Pulling the recent deploys. @ryan can you paste the instance template id so I can check instance_template.update events?

ryan (infra): instance-template: gpu-pool-template-v42 -> https://console.cloud/compute/instances?filter=name:gpu-pool*

ryan (infra): Recent terraform plan (from CI) shows change in module/gpu_pool/instance_type: "nvidia-t4-standard-8" => "a2-highmem-16g" by commit b3f9d1.

kai (eng-infra): That commit was merged into infra/opt branch earlier today; looks like a bad variable default got flipped. It should have been a test-only var.

ashwin (sre): Cool, root cause found. Why did autoscaler pick that type automatically though? Shouldn't the launch template specify a single machine type?

ryan (infra): Template was overwritten by the pipeline when the new var default leaked. Autoscaler respects template. Also saw preemption policy set to "none" in the template (so not preemptible), which explains cost.

devops-bot: CI pipeline triggered rollback job: infra/opt b3f9d1 -> rollback; status: queued

marta (oncall): While rollback runs, we should stop further launches. I patched the autoscaler to min=0 and disabled scale-ups for that pool (manually set scaleDownOnly=true).

kai (eng-infra): Nice one. Can we cordon/drain the expensive nodes to avoid new work and migrate active batches? Need a graceful drain: annotate pods with toleration changes.

ashwin (sre): Draining now. Command: 
```
kubectl drain gpu-a2-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
kubectl drain gpu-a2-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

ryan (infra): Rollback applied, new template restored to nvidia-t4-standard-8 and preemptible=true. Instance group will replace nodes on next reconciliation.

billing-bot: UPDATE: projected hourly spend dropping back toward baseline. Estimated saved $2.3k in the next hour.

marta (oncall): Postmortem TODOs: 1) revert bad var default in infra repo (done), 2) add terraform validation gate to prevent non-preemptible templates for this pool, 3) add policy to prevent memory-optimized GPU families for autoscale pools unless explicitly opt-in, 4) billing ticket and invoice hold request.

kai (eng-infra): Also recommend autoscaler guardrail: explicit allowed_instance_families whitelist and a hard limit on per-node hourly price. "If unit_price > $X -> fail deployment".

ashwin (sre): Filing the internal incident and cost ticket now. Tagging @finance for invoice hold.

ryan (infra): Quick patch: apply terraform plan to re-create instance group with preemptible=true now. Will monitor until replacements are up.

marta (oncall): Nodes cordoned and workload shifted. No errors in logs for inference pods so far.

kai (eng-infra): Thanks all. Follow-up: add an alert to detect machine-family drift (label vs allowed list) so this doesn't silently slip through.

billing-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Final estimate: net overage ~$8.1k (after rollback & preemptible replacements); ticket #BILL-3742 opened.

ashwin (sre): Long term: add terraform sentinel or policy checks in CI + runtime admission check in cluster autoscaler controller. Assigning action items in the incident doc.

kai (eng-infra): Great. Closing thread once finance confirms invoice hold. :thumbsup:
